svg.text: ESP32-S3 pin assignments, recovered from the stock firmware image
button DOWN; held at boot = updater escape hatch
button UP; held at boot = USB console mode
OUTPUT, LOW at boot, never written again
SD card detect, LOW = card present
• gpio_get_level() names exactly {6,12,13,16,40} plus the ISR argument
• The remaining pins (1,2,3,4,5,8,9,10,14,18,36,37,43,44) are claimed by
peripheral drivers, which is why they never appear in a gpio_config().
Two I²C masters, side by side
Bus 0 (display only): port 0, SDA 18 / SCL 10, 1 MHz, XTAL clock source,
glitch-ignore 7, internal pull-up OFF in stock (external pull-ups required
at 1 MHz), devices 0x38 (command) and 0x39 (data), disable_ack_check set on
both, one byte per transaction, 1000 ms timeout.
Bus 1 (sensors): port 1, SDA 8 / SCL 9, 400 kHz, XTAL clock source, glitch-
ignore 7, internal pull-up OFF, devices 0x60 (TUSB320) and 0x51 (PCF8563).
Footnote: the display bus runs with the SoC's internal pull-ups disabled —
the board must carry external pull-ups on GPIO18/GPIO10 to meet the 1 MHz
Stock boot-time GPIO drive order (not numeric pin order)
this is the earliest hardware GPIO action of the whole boot, before the I²C buses, the RTC, the boot-mode fork and the display, on every boot path
Every value is what the firmware writes, not what a meter reads. No pin here has been mapped to a pad on the J6/J7 spring-pin footprints, to a test
point, or to a connector contact; that mapping has no evidence and is out of scope.
